data.narrative:
Spaceium is a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by experienced propulsion and orbital mechanics engineers (CEO Ashi Dissanayake, CTO Reza Fetanat) with combined backgrounds spanning NASA, university research, and legacy engine development. The company has raised $6.3M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector includes 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and approximately 8 private peers at various stages.

Valuation analysis is constrained by data availability. The Peer-Median method is not applicable; only one same-stage private comparable exists, falling short of the three-point minimum for reliable triangulation. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied without Spaceium's revenue figure, which is typical for pre-revenue or early-stage private companies. The only viable method is Stage-Progression, which applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $6.3M total raised as a proxy for fair seed-stage valuation, yielding $15.75M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13–$18M, centered on $16M. This range reflects the stage-progression estimate and reasonable variance around it, but is narrow in confidence due to reliance on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include actual revenue traction (which would enable public-comp anchoring), the timeline to Series A (which affects the appropriate step-up multiple), and differentiation relative to better-capitalized peers like SpaceX and Rocket Lab. Additional disclosure of near-term milestones would materially improve valuation confidence.
